dod_intent_evidence: Air Force AFWERX SBIR/STTR Phase II contract ($1.8M, awarded July 2025 following Phase I success) for self-healing software supply chain innovations, plus a dedicated Lineaje Federal product line targeting cATO — news section and their own /federal page.
score_evidence: '10 Seconds To discover every instance of a zero-day' / '90% Reduction in vulnerability remediation effort' / '408+ Billion Open-source security data points tracked' → lab_language_intensity (stat-dropping SaaS marketing with zero warfighter framing on the main pages)

'Streamline the path to continuous Authority to Operate (cATO)' plus explicit EO14028/CISA-attestation language → deployment_awareness_absence very low, this company sells compliance/ATO tooling to others

'Software should continuously know what's inside, what's changed, what's vulnerable, and how to fix itself, so organizations can continuously trust what they build' → operator_absence (product literature never names a warfighter, operator, or field trainer — the customer is a security/compliance team)
Only open role: 'Product Builder / AI Product Manager' (San Francisco) → hiring_profile_skew (product-focused, neither pure-research nor field/compliance)

$1.8M Phase II following Phase I success (2025), alongside $27M total raised (Seed+Series A) and existing commercial/federal revenue via Carahsoft → stage_pressure lower, diversified revenue softens one-contract existential risk

blind_spots.blind_spot: Product architecture assumes continuous cloud connectivity to a centralized threat-intel catalog
blind_spots.operator_reality: The self-healing pitch (auto-source safe dependencies, auto-fix containers) depends on live access to Lineaje's 408B-datapoint cloud intelligence; a classified or air-gapped DoD software factory — the exact environment where fielded warfighter code actually gets built — can't reach that cloud, so the 'auto-fix' story stops working precisely where the AFWERX contract's self-healing goal matters most.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Built as multi-tenant SaaS for commercial and general federal customers first; the AFWERX Phase II is adapting that architecture to a DoD-specific self-healing use case, and the site never addresses an air-gapped deployment mode.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Continuously source safe dependencies and auto-fix source code and containers to ensure ongoing governance, provenance, attestation and risk elimination.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Autonomous code remediation is marketed without addressing government change-control/re-accreditation
blind_spots.operator_reality: Once a DoD system holds an ATO, any code change — even an automated vulnerability fix — typically triggers a POA&M or re-review; a vendor promising fully autonomous 'self-heal source code and containers' at scale needs an answer for how that survives the change-control gate on an already-accredited system, or the fixes just pile up unapproved.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The autonomous-remediation pitch is optimized to impress commercial DevSecOps buyers who control their own deploy pipeline, not government ISSOs who don't.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Self-heal source code and containers​Auto-detect poisoned software supply chains

blind_spots.blind_spot: Sells a path to cATO for customers without stating its own product's accreditation level
blind_spots.operator_reality: A tool meant to run inside a DoD software factory to remediate fielded code needs its own ATO at the right impact level (IL4/IL5) before a program will let it near production; the federal page pitches the customer's cATO journey but never states where Lineaje's own product sits on that ladder.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The federal marketing page is written to sell the value proposition (helping others reach cATO) rather than disclose Lineaje's own accreditation status, which may still be in progress.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Streamline the path to continuous Authority to Operate (cATO)

opener_hook: Your AFWERX Phase II builds on Phase I success for self-healing software supply chain remediation — worth comparing notes on how autonomous container fixes survive change control on a system that already holds an ATO.
what_they_do: Sells full-lifecycle software supply chain security software (SBOM management, vulnerability remediation, 'self-healing' open-source dependency fixes) to commercial and federal customers, with a dedicated AFWERX-funded R&D track for autonomous DoD remediation.
